journey: The life of a program: all ten subjects
journeyNote: The ten subjects aren't ten piles of loose facts — they are the life of a single program, from the moment it is written to the moment it learns from data on its own: first it gets organized, then it runs on hardware and is hosted by the kernel, talks to the outside world, puts its data on disk, outgrows a single machine, gets written as a service in a language built for the job, and truly goes to work — with math underneath it the whole way.

routeBlurbs.ai: Then, programs that learn from data: how backpropagation deals out blame to every weight, and how attention and the KV cache decide how fast — and how expensive — a model runs.
routeBlurbs.backend: Then see how services actually run: packaged into containers, orchestrated on a cluster, released down a pipeline, and — when something breaks — tracked to the root cause with logs, metrics, and traces. The four everyday jobs of backend engineering.
routeBlurbs.co: Then go one level down to the hardware: instructions, pipelines, caches, and how values are represented in memory — this is where why code is fast, or slow, is decided.
routeBlurbs.coding: Finish in Interview Practice: write the algorithms for real in the browser, run the tests, and check the complexity.
routeBlurbs.data: Then how data is stored: B+ tree indexes, transactions, and logs — the foundation under every backend service.
routeBlurbs.distributed: Leave the single machine behind: how many machines, amid latency, partitions, and timeouts that lie, still manage to agree on one shared version of the facts.
routeBlurbs.dsa: Start by drilling how data is organized — lookup, sorting, and graph algorithms — until they are muscle memory: how data is laid out, and what each operation costs, is the basic skill every later subject leans on.
routeBlurbs.go: Pick up a backend language along the way: why Go keeps the language so small, bakes concurrency into the syntax, and uses interfaces and composition instead of inheritance.
routeBlurbs.math: Fit the math foundations in at this point: probability and expectation are the language for understanding model behaviour and A/B tests — and the groundwork for the next subject, AI.
routeBlurbs.network: Add the network: requests, connections, and streaming — the machinery LLM APIs and inference services run on every day.
routeBlurbs.os: Next, how programs are hosted, scheduled, and protected by the operating system — every later question about performance and concurrency grows out of this.

routeNote: Suggested order: start with data structures & algorithms, then computer architecture and operating systems, followed by computer networks, data storage, and distributed systems; then the Go language and backend engineering; fit the math in just before artificial intelligence; and finish with real practice in the interview drills.
